prompt: Name a country in the G7.
source: G7 Information Centre, University of Toronto: https://www.g7.utoronto.ca/
valueLogic: The United States, United Kingdom, France and Germany come immediately. Japan is next. Italy and Canada form the tail - Canada because it joined a year after the others, Italy because people simply forget it.
note: England is accepted for the United Kingdom: strictly wrong, but the intent is unambiguous and busting on it would read as pedantry. The EU attends every summit but isn't one of the seven, so it's a non-busting distractor.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: The largest economy in the group, and a founding member in 1975.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: A founding member, and host of the third summit, in London in 1977.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Convened the first summit at Rambouillet in 1975 and hosted again at Evian in 2026.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: A founding member, attending as West Germany until reunification.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The only member outside Europe and North America.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: A founding member, and the most frequently forgotten of the six originals.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Joined in 1976, turning the G6 into the G7, and the single hardest to name.

distractors.name: European Union
distractors.note: Attends every summit but is not one of the seven member countries.

distractors.name: Russia
distractors.note: A member from 1998 until its suspension in 2014, when the G8 went back to being the G7.

distractors.name: China
distractors.note: Not a member, despite the size of its economy.

distractors.name: Australia
distractors.note: Not a member, though frequently invited as a guest.

distractors.name: South Korea
distractors.note: Not a member, though frequently invited as a guest.

distractors.name: India
distractors.note: Not a member, though frequently invited as a guest.
